sentences.text: Today we will talk about Zambia.
Zambia is a peaceful, green, and natural country in Southern Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Zambia?
Zambia is in Southern Africa.
It is next to Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Namibia, Angola, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
It is a landlocked country, so it has no ocean, but many rivers and lakes.
What is the capital city of Zambia?
The capital city is Lusaka.
Lusaka is in the South Central part of the country.
It is a busy city with offices, markets, and schools.
It is the largest city in Zambia.
Other towns include Ndola and Kitwe in the Copper Belt region, Living Stone near Victoria Falls, Chapata near the Malawi border.
How many people live in Zambia?
About 20 million people live in Zambia.
Many people live in cities, but others live in villages and farming areas.
Zambia has over 70 ethnic groups and many local traditions.
What language do people speak in Zambia?
The official language is English.
English is used in schools, business, and government.
People also speak many local languages, such as Bemba Nyanja, Chua, Tongalosi, Kaande, and more.
Most Zambians speak two or more languages.
What is the weather like in Zambia?
Zambia has a tropical climate.
Rainy season, November to April.
Cool, dry season, May to August.
Hot, dry season, September to October.
The land is green in the rainy season and dry in other times.
What does Zambia look like?
Zambia has rivers like the Zambezi River Waterfalls, like the famous Victoria Falls Hills, forests, and plains.
National Parks and Wildlife Reserves.
It is one of the best places in Africa for nature and safari.
What animals live in Zambia?
Zambia has many wild animals, such as elephants, lions, and leopards, buffalo, giraffes, and zebras, crocodiles and hippos in the rivers, birds like eagles, cranes, and hornbills.
People visit Zambia for wildlife tours and nature trips.
What do people eat in Zambia?
Zambian food is simple, natural, and filling.
People eat Nshima, thick -mayed porridge, main food, vegetables like rape, kale, and pumpkin leaves, beans, groundnuts, and sweet potatoes.
Fish, chicken, or beef, when available.
Popular dishes, Nshima with relish.
Relish can be meat, beans, or vegetables.
Capenta, small dried fish.
Ifeshashi, vegetables, and peanut sauce.
Chikanda, a local snack made from wild orchid root, also called African Polyne.
What do people drink in Zambia?
People drink water and herbal tea.
Mahiu, a fermented maize drink.
Milk, juice, and soda.
Adults may drink Chibuku, a local beer made from maize or sorghum.
People often share drinks in a friendly and social way.
What is life like in Zambia?
Life in Zambia is community -centered, calm and traditional.
People enjoy spending time with family, working on farms or in towns, visiting friends and neighbors, dancing and singing at events, going to church, which is very important to many people.
People help each other and enjoy living together peacefully.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, October 24th, Heroes Day and Unity Day, in July, Christmas and Easter, big Christian holidays.
Traditional ceremonies like kuremboka, lozi people, when the king moves from lowlands to highlands.
Weddings and festivals with music, drums, and dancing.
Traditional clothes are worn at special events and cultural days.
Some fun facts about Zambia.
Victoria Falls is one of the largest waterfalls in the world.
The Zambezi River forms the border with Zimbabwe.
The flag is green with an eagle, orange, black, and red stripes.
Zambia is one of the safest countries in Africa.
Zambians love football.
The national team is called Chippalopolo, the copper bullets.
Now you know many things about Zambia.
You know where it is, what people eat, and how they live.
You learned about Victoria Falls and Shima and Zambian culture.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
